A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VibeCheck. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching material across substantial display changes and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original vibe discovery, model-matching and preference-prediction experiments on HC3, Chatbot Arena, summarization, mathematics and captioning.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The discovery, clustering/reduction, two-judge validation, position swapping, filtering and error-driven iteration procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D. The shortened main-text discovery prompt is an explanatory paraphrase.

E1.justification: Both versions use HC3, Chatbot Arena overall/STEM/writing, CNN/DailyMail, correctly answered MATH problems with chain-of-thought responses, and COCO/ShareGPT-4V captions. No new dataset, task or test population is introduced.

E2.justification: The predefined-vibe baseline and one- versus three-iteration VibeCheck comparisons remain identical in v1 Table 3 and v4 Table 2. The models compared within each application also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 1 changes its illustrated model-identity accuracy criterion for a differentiating vibe from greater than 70% to greater than 55%. The experimental splits, judges, budgets and operational filtering thresholds in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A remain unchanged; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The iteration comparison, qualitative examples and judge-error cases are retained. v4 Figure 3 juxtaposes STEM/writing results already displayed separately in v1; the accompanying interpretation does not establish a new ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v1 Tables 7–14 and 16 report per-vibe model-matching and preference-regression p-values. v4 removes these tables, and its replacement figures omit both sets of p-values, despite Section 5 still promising them. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Headline accuracies remain unchanged, but v4 removes the model-matching coefficient entries from v1 Tables 7–16. Figure 17 newly reports COCO per-vibe Cohen’s kappa and changes displayed preference results: Contextual Storytelling has coefficient -13.514 in v1 Table 15 but a positive bar in v4. These are reporting changes, not demonstrated performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of vibe scores, separability and regression-based evaluation remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim automatic discovery and measurement of well-defined, differentiating, user-aligned vibes, alignment with human-discovered traits, approximately 80% model identification and 61% preference prediction, and applicability across the same three application domains.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds explicit task-dependent preference interpretations and qualifies them as preliminary evidence without individual-level comparisons. It also softens the explanation of lower STEM accuracy to a suspicion. However, its new statement that formality positively correlates with writing preference contradicts Figure 3’s negative writing coefficient.

D1.justification: v4 adds a VibeCheck code-repository link in the abstract and a Chatbot Arena dataset-access link in Section 5.2; v1 describes obtaining those battles from maintainers. The implementation descriptions, prompts and hyperparameter tables are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Lin et al. (2014) Microsoft COCO reference and associated citations. The existing related-work coverage and positioning of VibeCheck relative to earlier approaches otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits and tightens the prose, reorganizes the experimental overview and limitations, expands captions, and moves the example appendix. The main narrative structure and most methodological and technical-appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the overview and vibe displays, introducing colored low/high descriptions and signed bars. It consolidates the Arena accuracy table, adds joint STEM/writing and MATH displays of existing results, replaces detailed numerical appendix tables with compact figures, and relocates examples and the predefined-vibe list.

improvement.justification: Clearer displays and new code/data pointers improve usability, but removing numerical regression tables and coefficient p-values weakens scrutiny of the central preference associations. The new discussion also misstates the direction of writing preference for formality relative to Figure 3. With the principal experiments unchanged, these losses in evidential transparency and interpretive accuracy produce a modest net decline.
